items.title: Women’s representation in senior corporate roles falls; Avtar flags US DEI pullback
items.summary: Women’s share of Corporate Executive roles among Best Companies falls to 16.7% from 20%; Avtar managing director Saundarya Rajesh says US policy changes have had a “very strong impact” on women in India

items.title: Double deflation debate over GDP methodology no ‘great battle’: Niti Ayog Vice Chairman
items.summary: Private capital expenditure (capex) cycle to gain significant momentum once capacity utilisation in the private corporate sector reaches 80%, up from the current 70–75% levels.

items.title: NMDC raises lump ore price by ₹150/tonne, holds price of fines
items.summary: The new price is ₹5,400 per tonne

items.title: Public Accounts Committee flags failure to transfer ₹9,222 crore in cess collections to designated reserve funds
items.summary: Members question the Finance Ministry’s explanation; panel chief K.C. Venugopal says cess proceeds must not be used to finance fiscal deficit instead of their intended purpose

items.title: India has 51 days coal stocks to meet power demand; production recovers after monsoon disruption
items.summary: The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) had observed recently that 53 thermal power-plants were holding 25% or less than their overall coal requirements.

items.title: Govt puts bank staff performance-linked incentive scheme on hold ahead of strike
items.summary: The decision followed a meeting between Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and a delegation of bank employees

items.title: What prompted India’s return to the ‘A’ rating after 35 years?
items.summary: While most sovereign credit rating agencies rate India a grade or two above ‘junk’ status, the recent upgrade by the Japan Credit Rating Agency sees India return to the ‘A’ grade for the first time since early 1988

items.title: LPG booking interval for rural consumers cut to 25 days from 45
items.summary: This brings the interval between bookings for rural consumers on par with urban consumers, for whom the period remains unchanged at 25 days

items.title: Govt spurs coal rake loading by 20% to strengthen stocks positions at thermal plants
items.summary: CEA data indicates 53 domestic coal-fired plants were operating with less than 25% of their critical normative requirements as on September 5

items.title: C. Rangarajan flags fewer regional rural banks as ‘a step in the wrong direction’; urges RBI to incentivise SFBs
items.summary: Former RBI Governor says consolidation risks eroding RRBs’ local character; says 11 small finance banks will not meet the sector’s unmet credit needs

items.title: Does ‘inflation targeting’ work in India?
items.summary: India’s Phillips curve is found to be flat, while households’ inflation expectations remain consistently higher than the RBI’s projections; this suggests that inflation targeting can lower output and employment without a commensurate reduction in inflation

items.title: India’s unemployment data dilemma
items.summary: A fall in unemployment may indicate distress-driven entry into low-productivity jobs rather than genuine employment creation

items.title: Gold and silver rise
items.summary: Short-term trend in gold and silver have turned positive post the breakout of key resistance level; the trend would remain positive until the support level is breached

items.title: Coal production re-accelerates amid easing monsoon; daily output rises to 1.7 MT
items.summary: Coal India’s sizeable inventory position as a cushion against supply disruptions. The improvement in production and dispatch amid easing monsoon offers greater flexibility, supporting higher supplies to power sector.

items.title: India Prices $10 Billion of Equity Deals in August, a Record Month
items.summary: India priced almost $10 billion of equity deals in August, its best month ever, led by the government's LIC stake sale.

items.title: Wipro Stock Falls as Nifty 50 Exit Looms
items.summary: Wipro's removal follows a severe share-price decline as investors reassess how generative AI may reshape Indian technology services.

items.title: India's Tech Mahindra gains as strong deal wins lift growth outlook
items.summary: Shares of India's Tech Mahindra rose as much as 3.5% on ‌Friday after the IT services firm ‌posted better-than-expected quarterly revenue, with analysts saying strong deal wins ​and margin improvement could make it one of the fastest growing companies among its peers.  The stock was last up 1.8% at 1,537.5 rupees ‌and was among ⁠the top gainers on the Nifty IT index, which was trading 1% ⁠higher.  It was also one of the top gainers on the benchmark Nifty 50 index.

items.title: India regains favor as investors seek shelter from AI-driven market swings
items.summary: Investing.com -- Indian equities are attracting renewed interest from global investors as concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence-driven rally prompt a shift toward markets viewed as more defensive, Bloomberg reported.

items.title: India's fifth spot in global market cap list under threat as Taiwan closes in
items.summary: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M May 26 (Reuters) - India's position as the fifth-largest global market by capitalisation is under threat as Taiwan closes in on the South Asian nation's spot,

items.title: Worsening food inflation warrants policy moves before household hardship reaches far and wide
items.summary: Inflation is within its acceptable limits, but it’s the upward trend that policymakers need to worry about. Food prices especially. With farms hit by patchy rains amid new oil shockwaves, the Centre must protect Indian households that see food eating up almost half their domestic budget.

items.title: Will asset tokenization live up to its promise? Here's what India must do for Demat 2.0 to succeed
items.summary: Launched by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), Demat 2.0 has seen some high-profile tokenized bond issuances. Tokenization holds the promise of a superior market, but we can’t take its success for granted. Here's what must be done.

items.title: We have an El Niño tracker in space but the rainfall reshapers we need to study most are closer home
items.summary: India has satellite data to help track rainfall and inflation risks arising from global tilts in oceanic warmth. The country’s challenge is to study atmospheric aberrations closer home—such as the Indian Ocean dipole and winter rain distortions.

items.title: Voice to capital: What India’s Brics summit leaves behind
items.summary: Brics needs to make investment in emerging markets easier to understand, easier to de-risk and more attractive to both domestic and global capital.

items.title: Voice of the Global South: Can Brics do more than vocalize a vision for the world order?
items.summary: Can the group’s shared dissatisfaction with today’s world order yield institutions that actually deliver? That will depend on how well the 11 members of Brics are able to cooperate on achieving tangible outcomes.

items.title: UPI’s  ₹16,000 crore MDR windfall could change the economics of digital payments
items.summary: Historically, UPI generated negligible direct revenue for payment apps; however, potential MDR of  ₹16,000 crore is reshaping the landscape. This revenue could enhance bank capacities and provide UPI apps new resources to attract consumers and merchants, helping evolving the payment ecosystem.

items.title: Time for a fraud risk index? Credible readings could help investors track the risk of corporate fraud
items.summary: Indian investors go by risk-reward ratios and may look at credit ratings as well, but we have no objective way to capture the risk of being scammed. Here’s how research on fraud could be used as a basis to craft an unbiased index that would help secure investors.

items.title: The internet age can bridge what tongues divide
items.summary: Modi's choice of Hindi reflects its importance in connecting with younger generations. With 610 million speakers globally, Hindi’s growth illustrates a potential national identity. The emergence of a hybrid language could unite various cultures in the digital age.

items.title: The OECD's school report obfuscates a global education emergency instead of raising the alarm—why?
items.summary: Despite a collapse in learning outcomes across the world, the OECD’s report on one of the world’s best known surveys has glossed over what’s clearly a crisis. It’s now for educationists to raise an alarm over the impact of technology on cognitive capacity.

items.title: Tata Sons: To list or not to list may no longer be a question—but whether it’s for the better still is
items.summary: What to expect if Tata Sons goes public as directed by RBI? The historical record—from Ford’s story in the US to the family-run chaebol of South Korea—is too mixed to form a clear view. Will public answerability favour better outcomes? It could go either way.

items.title: Should conglomerate holding companies be listed?
items.summary: The case for listing Tata Sons is gaining urgency, but a public listing is no cure-all.

items.title: Should America cut Social Security? Here's why this support system remains critical even now
items.summary: Critics argue that this programme, also known as Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance, is too generous. But that isn't necessarily the case. It’s only outdated, but it remains an important solution to current problems.

items.title: RBI: How a more transparent and predictable supervisory architecture could strengthen confidence in its decisions
items.summary: RBI’s enforcement has a rigorous process, but penalty cases in the news have stirred a debate on whether India needs an appellate authority. Its supervisory role is relatively opaque for valid reasons, but RBI may find that the more predictable and proportionate it is, the better.

items.title: Monetary skew: RBI must not let its liquidity moves work against its rate-setting panel’s decisions
items.summary: A dollar deluge has placed the Reserve Bank of India's liquidity management in focus and instances of it being out of whack with the monetary policy committee's interest-rate decisions suggest it might be time to revisit the latter’s remit.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | The UPI platform must pay for itself, sure, but let’s also promote India’s digital rupee
items.summary: A fee on merchant transactions via the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has left many dismayed, although this regime will be lightly applied. Regardless of the move’s impact, it’s time to popularize the e-rupee, a central bank digital currency waiting in the wings.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | Retail inflation has been above RBI’s target for three months in a row: time to act?
items.summary: With consumer inflation at 4.8% in August and both El Nino and an oil shock raising risks, it may be time for India’s central bank to pull out its monetary toolbox. The economy’s strong pace of growth grants RBI the space for a hawkish move.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | Never mind America’s reaction: why Brics should become a global rule-shaper
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for the group to evolve from a taker of rules to one that shapes them is aligned with India’s interests as well as the world’s. The power structure of multilateral institutions, for example, must reflect today’s global reality

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | India’s August trade data reveals robust export shipments in spite of rough seas
items.summary: The country's merchandise exports rose sharply last month to $43.8 billion against steep odds. Global woes are far from over, with oil prices and bond yields soaring, but India’s trade pacts could help retain this fiscal year’s export momentum.

items.title: Learning on the job is crucial for certain professions but AI threatens to automate it away
items.summary: Lawyers and mathematicians have something in common—AI has invaded tasks that exercise the mental faculties of learners. It's wise not to adopt AI blindly in fields where working problems out is at the heart of professional knowledge acquisition.

items.title: India’s ‘missing’ trillions in nominal GDP are not a mystery but the result of a statistical upgrade
items.summary: Questions have arisen over India’s GDP data for the first quarter of 2026-27, but we should let the numbers do the talking. Downward revisions of past data are explained by better calculations while today’s economic momentum is hard to dispute.

items.title: India’s semiconductor opportunity lies beyond the fab
items.summary: Advanced packaging could give India a lower-capital pathway to semiconductor manufacturing—and help build the talent and systems ecosystem needed to compete globally.

items.title: India’s IT services industry could get a slice of the AI revenue pie as value migrates to what it excels at
items.summary: As basic AI models become more replaceable, the layer that adapts them for enterprise use gains in value. This is the business that Indian IT firms must aim for, bringing together their knowledge of global enterprises, regulatory requirements and expertise.

items.title: India should aim to attract at least $100 billion a year in net FDI—but much reform work must be done for that
items.summary: The country should aim to attract FDI that can embed India in global value chains, build export capacity, transfer technology and create competitive domestic supply chains. However, turning globally competitive to join value chains requires reform action on many key fronts simultaneously.

items.title: India has drawn dollars in bulk but faces a policy quadrilemma—one that involves asset values too
items.summary: The macro policy trilemma is well known, but India actually faces a quadrilemma. Here's why asset inflation also needs to be managed while considering trade-offs. There is some evidence that Indian assets remain largely overpriced.

items.title: Governance lesson: A good government is recognized by how effectively it ensures good outcomes, not the power it wields
items.summary: Tragedies like the recent collapse of an unauthorized building in Delhi's Satya Niketan is a call for greater state capacity rather than more displays of control which shift the burden of safety onto those being regulated. An even more complex maze of rules isn’t the answer.

items.title: Dani Rodrik: Services have served us a surprise revolution of productivity across the world
items.summary: Globally, services have turned more productive than economists expected, but the benefits of it are not widely shared. Policy measures need to kick in for productivity gains to uplift lives all around—but without getting in the way of this revolution.

items.title: Chaos ahead? Grand investments in AI going bad might set off a painful chain of events
items.summary: Massive loans taken to finance enormous investments in data centres and other AI-related fields could go bad if demand for AI fails expectations. From high net-worth individuals to banks, pension funds and even university endowments, many stand to suffer harsh blows if a bubble bursts.

items.title: Capital formation uptick: is India on the verge of an investment supercycle after a long wait?
items.summary: Overall investment is picking up in the country and so is private participation. It may be too early to judge, but a swelter of risks must be faced down for India’s gross fixed capital formation to sustainably expand its share of GDP.

items.title: Brics’ New Delhi Declaration gives the business community of the Global South something rare
items.summary: Although declarations are commitments, the one made last week by Brics under India's chairship is a victory for Indian diplomacy that sets out a path for equitable growth. Brics’s real test, though, lies in the working groups, action plans and pilot projects that must now follow.

items.title: Beyond the unicorn: why India needs a real innovation index
items.summary: A National Innovation Index would score startups on innovation and inclusive growth. A National Transmission Index would score the government on delivery. Together, they would form a closed, positive-feedback loop that accelerates the economy towards Viksit Bharat.

items.title: As India urbanizes, rural places reclassified as urban should not deprive anyone of welfare benefits
items.summary: A binary classification of areas as urban or rural doesn’t reflect today’s reality of urbanization, but state programmes still go by it. This could result in abrupt cut-offs from schemes that vulnerable households depend on. Here's what policymakers should consider that’s both doable and just.

items.title: Anthropic's warnings of a possible AI doom scenario are out of whack with its endeavours
items.summary: The artificial intelligence (AI) firm founded by Dario Amodei likes to present itself as one of the ‘good guys’ of AI safety. But this moral self-certification is an odd justification for pushing ahead with risky AI systems.

items.title: Andy Mukherjee: Has Sebi lost its nerve on auctions for stock-market closing price discovery?
items.summary: There's no doubt India needs market depth, but its regulator seems to have given up on a reform it had instituted recently. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has asked for a discussion on whether to shorten the auction window or roll the idea back (effectively). This is disappointing

items.title: America versus China: headed for mutually assured doom? Not if they shake hands on AI safety
items.summary: Feverish talk of the two archrivals being trapped in a race of mutually assured destruction (MAD) may be exaggerated. Yet, they owe humanity the safety of mutual restraints on dangerous artificial intelligence (AI). Both must sit down and talk.

items.title: A sneaky attempt to save on childcare outlays could pit American parents against one another
items.summary: Although the US has a high proportion of children living in single-parent households, it lacks the social infrastructure offered by many other rich countries. Reworking subsidies in a way that would pit working parents against those who stay home would be a step backwards.
